business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Procurement of Battery-Grade Lithium Carbonate Powder

Double Taxation Agreement between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the Federal Republic of Germany (2012)
Double Taxation Agreement between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the French Republic (2018)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (consolidated version incorporating the Law of 23 December 2022); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners, as amended by the Law of 23 December 2022; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2019 on the functioning and access to the Register of Beneficial Owners; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended (SCSp provisions).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority or notary public in the UBO's country of nationality/residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if the origin country is a Hague Convention state) or Consular Legalization by a Luxembourg embassy/consulate (if not)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / official register extract of the corporate general partner (where applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial register or companies registry in the jurisdiction of incorporation of the GP (or Luxembourg Business Registers if GP is Luxembourg-domiciled)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for foreign extracts; LBR authentication for Luxembourg extracts

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement) for each UBO/manager/signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed utility provider or regulated financial institution in the document origin country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized certification followed by Hague Apostille / consular legalization (for private-issued documents, notarization in the origin country is required before apostille)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter for the corporate entity and its principals
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relationship bank or credit institution (regulated international bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required if issued by a bank directly; otherwise notarization and apostille optional as per the receiving Luxembourg bank policies

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney for the incorporation agent / legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public before whom each UBO/GP executes the power of attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (mandatory where the POA is used for registration with the LBR) or consular legalization for non-Hague countries

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Screening of all UBOs, directors, partners, managers and signatories against the Luxembourg FIU (CRF) consolidated sanctions and PEP lists, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UN Security Council sanctions (UNSCR 1267/1988/1718), and the OFAC SDN list. Screening is mandatory under the 2004 AML Law and CSSF Regulation 12-02. Continuous monitoring is required; enhanced due diligence shall be applied to any PEPs, family members and known close associates. Negative screening results must be documented and kept for at least 5 years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — e-RCS (electronic platform: www.lbr.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official language for LBR filings is French. A company name must use the Latin alphabet; any name originally in another alphabet must be transliterated into Latin characters. The legal form suffix 'SCSp' or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' is mandatory. The name must be distinctive, non-misleading, and may not include words contrary to public order or morality. Names identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name are refused.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: État/Lëtzebuerg/Luxembourg (prior ministerial approval where it implies an official state or public authority status)
Fonds/Fund (prohibited for non-regulated commercial entities unless CSSF authorization obtained)
Chambre de commerce (reserved to the Chamber of Commerce)
Crédit/Savings (requires CSSF or Ministry of Finance authorization as financial term)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant receives an official e-RCS refusal notice. Within 15 calendar days of the refusal, the applicant or its counsel may submit a reasoned administrative objection to the Head of Registration of the LBR, including evidence that the name is distinctive and not prohibited. The LBR must issue a decision within one month. If the objection is rejected, an annulment action may be brought before the Administrative Tribunal under the amended law of 1 December 1978 within 3 months of notification. During this period, the name remains blocked; a renewed application may be made after the objection is dismissed or by using a modified name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Professional domiciliation is legally permitted for an SCSp under Luxembourg law, but the registered office must be a genuine physical location in Luxembourg (not a mere PO Box). A 'virtual office' arrangement is acceptable only if provided by an approved domiciliation agent and if the partnership's books and records, management decisions and general partner's office are reasonably accessible in Luxembourg; otherwise, there is a risk that the SCSp is deemed managed from abroad, triggering a permanent establishment of its partners or loss of Luxembourg tax residency (tax transparency makes this especially relevant).
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15-25% estimated annual probability of unannounced on-site inspection by the Luxembourg social security (CCSS), ITM (labour inspection) or tax authorities for a medium-risk trading SCSp. Probability rises to >40% if the SCSp applies for a Luxembourg tax residence certificate, VAT registration, or has an annual turnover exceeding EUR 500,000.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting and notarisation of the SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; EUR 500–1,500 plus notary official fees; may be waived for private deed formation, but notarial form recommended.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of incorporation notice in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Ministry of Justice

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory filing fee (free of charge).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization of foreign identity and corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs (apostille) or embassy/consulate of Luxembourg in the origin country
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document consular fee (approx. EUR 50–150 per document), according to the Hague Convention / consular tariff schedules.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Approved domiciliation agent (adresse de domiciliation) registered with the LBR
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; typical annual fee EUR 1,200–2,500.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT initial due diligence and sanctions screening (incl. PEP check software)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Law firm or compliance service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; EUR 600–1,200 per file, plus licensed screening database fees.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal counsel and tax advice for pre-incorporation structuring
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm / tax advisor (registered with the Luxembourg Bar)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; EUR 250–500 per hour, 8–10 hours expected.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Extract from the RCS on non-registration of the chosen name
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee for an official information extract.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 101 to 107 (SCSp regime introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013); amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and on annual accounts.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Registration application of an SCSp filed electronically with the RCS, together with the executed partnership agreement (contrat de société) and the RCS-published excerpt in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum capital is required by law for an SCSp; the initial capital is freely determined in the partnership agreement. No statutory escrow or bank-blocked account requirement applies under the amended Law of 10 August 1915.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: First Resolution of the Managing General Partner (Gérant) of [SCSp Name] (the Partnership). The sole General Partner, acting as managing body, irrevocably resolves: 1. Subscription: to accept the initial partnership interests per the subscription schedule, with initial capital of [EUR amount] contributed by the partners. 2. Registered Office: to adopt the registered office at [address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. 3. Management: to appoint [Name] as Gérant with sole signature rights for the Partnership's day-to-day administration. 4. Administration: to authorize opening bank accounts and filing all registrations with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register, the VAT Administration, and the Register of Beneficial Owners. Effective immediately. Adopted in Luxembourg on [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Clearance and Drafting of the Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), RCS pre-registration name query desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a pre-registration name query to confirm that the proposed corporate name is distinguishable from existing RCS entries. Prepare the SCSp partnership agreement in English or French, covering identity of the general partner and limited partners, corporate object, registered office, capital commitments, profit-sharing, and termination provisions. If any contribution consists of real estate, arrange for a Luxembourg notary.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and corporate object description
Draft SCSp partnership agreement
Passport/ID copies and proof of residential address of all partners
Lease agreement or domiciliation letter for the registered office
For corporate partners: certificate of incorporation, authorizing board resolution, and list of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name query returns a conflict, select two alternative names and resubmit. The RCS does not formally reserve names; protection accrues upon filing, so expedite registration immediately after negative clearance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Formalization of the Partnership Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (notarial deed) or private deed with legalized signatures under Article 102 of the Law of 10 August 1915
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the final partnership agreement. If a private deed is used, legalize the signatures (apostille for foreign signatories) or have signatories appear before a Luxembourg notary. Ensure powers of attorney for corporate partners comply with Luxembourg formalities. Attach the subscription schedule confirming capital contributed by the general partner and each limited partner.
required_dossiers: Final executed partnership deed (acte de société)
Subscription schedule with capital amounts per partner
Power of attorney and certified identity documents
For foreign corporate partners: original commercial register extract from home jurisdiction
Apostilles or legalizations for all foreign executed documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defects in consent or execution are cured by re-executing the defective pages or by a supplementary notarial rectification deed (acte rectificatif). Signature discrepancies are cured with a fresh attestation of signature or reaffirmation before a notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration and Issuance of Corporate Identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), electronic filing via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the registration application electronically. Attach the executed deed, the mandatory list of partners, registered office details, identity of the gérant/general partner, and legalized signatures. Pay the statutory registration fee (approx. EUR 75) and publication charges. Upon admission, the RCS allocates the corporate registration number and the LEI code.
required_dossiers: Duly signed RCS registration form (e-signature equivalent)
Certified copy of the executed partnership deed
List of general and limited partners with contributed amounts
Consent of registered office provider or lease agreement
Identity documents and residence information of the gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues an inquiry (imputation), respond within 15 calendar days with clarifying documents. The Registrar may refuse registration only on legal grounds; any refusal is appealable before the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) sitting in commercial matters.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the RESA and Third-Party Opposability
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers — Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCS automatically forwards the statutory excerpt of incorporation for publication in RESA. Verify the published excerpt online for accuracy of the name, registered office, capital amounts, and manager details. Publication confers third-party opposability of the constitution documents and statutory representations.
required_dossiers: No active filing required — cross-posting by RCS
Online verification of the RESA excerpt (retain a dated screenshot)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Typographical errors in the published excerpt are corrected by a written request to the RCS. Substantive errors require a rectificatory deed and a further registration filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Operational Activation: Beneficial Ownership, VAT, Establishment Authorization and Banking
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Ministry of the Economy — Establishment Authorization Service; licensed bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of RCS registration, file the beneficial-owner declaration with the RBE, identifying the general partner and every limited partner holding more than 25% of partnership interests. Register for VAT with the AEDT if the procurement activity creates a Luxembourg VAT nexus. Apply for the general commercial authorization (autorisation d'établissement) under the amended Law of 2 September 2011 if the SCSp operates a trading office or warehouse. Open the operational bank account under enhanced due diligence for battery-metals arbitrage.
required_dossiers: RBE beneficial-owner declaration form
AEDT VAT registration form (where applicable)
Ministry of the Economy establishment permit application (if physical premises)
Bank KYC package: articles, RCS extract, UBO declaration, source-of-funds statement
Business plan and three-year projection for trade-finance and LC facilities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late RBE filings attract administrative fines; file promptly. VAT registration refusal is appealable to the AEDT Director and then to the administrative court. Banking rejection due to sanctions or PEP screening is cured by a detailed transaction-flow memorandum and evidence of lawful origin of lithium-carbonate stock.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg — Directorate General for Industry, Establishment Authorization Service (Service des autorisations d'établissement)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement — Merchant and Wholesale Trader Business Permit under the amended Law of 2 September 2011 regulating access to the professions of craftsperson, merchant, industrialist and certain liberal professions

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency) — Department of Environmental Assessments and Permits
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not subject to environmental impact assessment: the activity is office-based cross-border procurement and wholesale trading of battery-grade lithium carbonate powder, with no installation listed under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 8 June 1999 on classified installations. No EIA registration or development consent is triggered for the trading activity itself.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No production or stationary emission source exists. If a warehouse is later operated, the applicable regime is the amended Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management, requiring a waste-handling contract with an approved collector; VOC and wastewater thresholds of Directive 2010/75/EU are not triggered by wholesale trading of powders without reprocessing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For administrative offices, fire-safety conformity is certified by the lessor, and a favorable visit by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) is required before occupation if the premises exceed simple office use. Occupational clearance by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) requires a documented workplace risk assessment, first-aid equipment, and emergency evacuation arrangements in accordance with the amended Labor Code of Luxembourg.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes, ACD) – portal: eCDF (Electronic Corporate and Fiscal Declarations); VAT authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) – portal: myGuichet.lu / eTVA; business registry: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via eJustice
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing an SCSp must first obtain a 13-digit national identification number (matricule) by filing an incorporation deed with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through the eJustice portal, followed by automatic attribution of the matricule. Where no Luxembourg permanent establishment exists or where the entity does not hold real estate, the SCSp must nevertheless register for VAT (TVA) with the AEDT using Form No. 6401 (inscription au registre TVA) within 15 days of commencing taxable activity; a fixed place of business or economic nexus in Luxembourg triggers mandatory VAT registration. The VAT number is the matricule preceded by 'LU'. No separate federal TIN is required for partnerships; each partner's foreign TIN must be declared in the annual partnership return filed via eCDF.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible; the SCSp is a transparent entity for Luxembourg corporate income tax (IRC) and net wealth tax (IMF) purposes, unless it opts for joint taxation under Article 159 of the LIR or elects to be treated as a taxable entity. The SCSp is separately liable for VAT as a taxable person regardless of tax transparency.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Check-the-box-style election: Under Article 159 LIR, an SCSp may irrevocably elect corporate income taxation (transparent-to-nontransparent) by filing a joint declaration with its partners within the legal deadlines; alternatively, a hybrid mismatch election may be available under Article 168ter LIR to align Luxembourg classification with a foreign jurisdiction's classification (e.g., US check-the-box) provided the entity is not resident and is not a Luxembourg taxable entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 (no general VAT registration threshold for established EU businesses); a non-established EU/foreign business that supplies goods or services with a Luxembourg VAT nexus must register from the first euro of taxable turnover. For distance sales of goods to Luxembourg consumers, the EUR 10,000 EU-wide cross-border distance sales threshold applies only to EU-established suppliers under the OSS regime, and non-EU suppliers must register immediately.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg has not introduced mandatory real-time e-invoicing clearance or continuous transaction controls (CTC) for B2B domestic suppliers as of the knowledge cut-off; however, e-invoicing in Peppol or Factur-X format is mandatory for public sector B2G procurement under the Luxembourg e-Invoicing Law of 15 August 2021. All VAT-registered entities must submit periodic e-filing through the AEDT eTVA/MyGuichet portal, and SAF-T XML must be submitted on demand for audit purposes. Digital stamping is not yet mandatory, but the European Council adopted the VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) proposals requiring standard electronic invoicing for cross-border B2B transactions by 2030 and real-time digital reporting from 2035; no current deviating API clearance mandate exists.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of battery-grade lithium carbonate powder (CN code 2836.91) to non-EU destinations are zero-rated under Article 47(1)(a) LTV and Article 393 of the VAT Directive, provided (i) the goods are physically exported from Luxembourg or another EU Member State by the supplier or a third party acting on its behalf, (ii) the supplier retains proof of export within 90 days and proof of arrival in the third country, and (iii) the purchaser is not established in Luxembourg. Intra-EU supplies to VAT-registered customers are exempt with right to deduction under Article 41 LTV (Intra-Community supply), requiring the customer's valid EU VAT number and an Intrastat declaration threshold compliance. Offshore services linked to international trade (e.g., logistics) may be zero-rated under the place-of-supply rules if supplied to a non-EU business customer, but pure trading commissions or procurement services supplied to a non-EU business are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT rather than zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic Export Declaration via LU Customs - Douanes et Accises, SAD/declaration IE507)
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Airway Bill (AWB) naming the Luxembourg exporter/seller and consignee as the non-EU buyer
Inward Remittance Certificate / proof of payment evidencing actual receipt of export proceeds by the Luxembourg exporter (bank SWIFT confirmation or foreign exchange settlement statement)
Proof of Transport (e.g., CMR waybill if road transport; transport contract or container tracking evidence)
Proof of exit from EU customs territory (customs stamp or post-export customs status confirmation)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under Articles 456-461 LIR and VAT enforcement rules, fraudulent export zero-rating (e.g., fictitious exports, forged customs documents, missing proof of dispatch) triggers (i) retrospective VAT assessment and reversal of input VAT deduction, (ii) a 10% late payment interest per annum and administrative fines of up to EUR 10,000 for recording irregularities, and (iii) criminal penalties of imprisonment of up to 6 months and/or fine of up to EUR 25,000 for documentary forgery. Under the Luxembourg General Tax Procedure Act (Steueranpassungsgesetz, § 9-10), where a transaction mischaracterized as an export is found to be a sham, tax reassessment may be extended to 5 years (10 years for fraud), and VAT penalties may be doubled to 20% of the tax evaded. The AEDT and ACD maintain a mutual assistance framework for cross-border audit and exchange of information; clawback of input VAT recovered on export goods may also apply under Article 29(5) LIR substance requirements if the SCSp lacks economic substance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) acting within the Eurosystem in concert with the European Central Bank (ECB). The BCL operates the domestic real-time gross settlement component (LIPS-Gross / T2), compiles Luxembourg balance-of-payments statistics, and oversees payment system stability, while prudential supervision of credit institutions is vested in the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Fully convertible. Luxembourg is a euro-area member and applies Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) on free movement of capital together with Directive 88/361/EEC. No exchange-control authorization, FX allocation, prior licensing, or central bank permit is required for current-account payments (trade in lithium carbonate) or capital-account operations (subscription of SCSp partnership interests, shareholder loans, distributions, liquidation proceeds). Profit remittances to non-resident limited partners are unrestricted; because the SCSp is fiscally transparent, no Luxembourg withholding tax applies on distributions, and the paying bank applies only standard EU/UN sanctions screening and enhanced due diligence appropriate to a medium-risk commodity-trading entity. There are no prohibitions on maintaining foreign-currency accounts domestically or offshore, nor any minimum financing or FX repatriation requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory timeline for repatriation of export proceeds, no mandatory conversion ratio into EUR, and no surrender requirement on foreign-currency receipts arising from international trade. A Luxembourg-resident entity receiving cross-border payments exceeding statistical thresholds is, however, subject to balance-of-payments reporting obligations to the BCL (Eurosystem framework), which is a purely statistical filing duty and does not restrict the ownership, use, or disposition of foreign currency.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account (EUR)
Operational Account (EUR/USD multi-currency) and Documentary Trade Finance (L/C) facility
Operational Account and Commodity Trade Finance line (L/C, guarantees, USD clearing)
Operational Account (EUR) and Escrow Account for capital subscriptions
Operational Account (multi-currency incl. USD) with strong New York correspondent clearing

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Limited and auxiliary only. A fintech EMI lawfully operating in Luxembourg must hold a CSSF e-money licence or a valid EU/EEA passport notification under PSD2; UK- or non-EU-headquartered platforms without such passport cannot lawfully serve a Luxembourg SCSp. Even when licensed, digital EMIs are generally unsuitable as primary rails for ISIC 4662 commodity settlements: they lack substantive SWIFT correspondent relationships for USD-denominated lithium-carbonate drawings, cannot issue or confirm commercial letters of credit under UCP 600, and frequently classify partnership treasury flows with multiple third-party payees as elevated risk. Feasibility rating for mobilization expenses and small-ticket operational payments: Medium; as primary settlement and clearing infrastructure: Low.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No absolute statutory mandate for physical attendance exists. Luxembourg's amended AML law (Law of 12 November 2004, as amended, and CSSF Regulation 12-02) permits remote client identification using an eIDAS-compliant qualified electronic identification/digital KYC mechanism. In practice, for a newly formed SCSp with a non-Luxembourg corporate general partner, tier-1 institutions uniformly require at least a video identification session and frequently an initial in-person interview at the Luxembourg branch attended by the general partner's authorised signatory (and, where applied, the ultimate beneficial owner). The SCSp lacks separate legal personality, so the bank opens the account in the name of the partnership with the general partner acting; full look-through CDD is applied to the GP and every limited partner irrespective of participation percentage, and remote-only onboarding of a HK/SG corporate GP is commercially difficult in the absence of an existing banking track record.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly formed, unregulated, tax-transparent SCSp with a foreign corporate general partner and opaque ultimate control chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed limited partnership agreement; private placement memorandum; Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) excerpt and certificate of registration; statutory UBO declaration; constitutional documents, board resolutions and registers of directors/UBOs of the GP and each corporate limited partner; delegation-of-authority matrix; and a written commercial rationale memo describing the battery-metals procurement and arbitrage model between Chilean/Australian supply sources and EU/APAC battery manufacturers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds for capital injection: non-resident limited partners remitting substantial EUR/USD subscriptions into an unregulated partnership active in a commodity sector (trade-based money-laundering typology).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital call notices and individual LP subscription agreements matching exact wiring amounts; source-of-wealth file per LP comprising audited financial statements, tax returns and regulated-bank reference letters from the home jurisdiction; evidence of lawful provenance (dividend distributions, disposal proceeds, undrawn credit facilities); confirmation that no cash, bearer instruments, or crypto-asset conversion channels are involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border lithium-carbonate procurement chain involving Chinese suppliers, Chilean and Australian producers, and multimodal shipping routes raising invoice-manipulation concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master supply/offtake agreements governed by a recognized commercial law; per-transaction pack: commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, transport document (ocean B/L or CMR), insurance certificate, and third-party laboratory certificate of analysis confirming battery-grade Li2CO3 specification (purity >= 99.5% with controlled impurity profile); independent SGS/Bureau Veritas/Intertek pre-shipment inspection report; UCP 600-compliant document sets where L/Cs are used; end-user statement confirming delivery into EU battery cathode production.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure: counterparties domiciled in the People's Republic of China that may interact with EU, US, and UN restrictive-measures lists, including Russia/Belarus origin substitution risks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provenance certificate for every lot stating source mine, beneficiation plant, and exclusion of Russian/Belarusian origin; comprehensive batch-screening reports of all counterparties, vessels, insurance underwriters and intermediary banks against the EU Consolidated Sanctions List and OFAC SDN/Entity List; full corporate registry documentation, ownership chain and ultimate beneficial owners of each supplier; contractual compliance covenants; automated negative-news and list-screening SOP; anti-circumvention representations in each purchase agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High volume of third-party or geographically divergent payments (tolling fees to Switzerland, freight to Rotterdam, producer payments to Santiago) not obviously consistent with the stated trade route.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cash-flow forecast and treasury mandate letter mapping every outbound payment class to an underlying agreement; executed contracts with freight forwarders, warehousemen, insurers, and inspection agents; bank-statement-to-invoice reconciliation trail for the preceding 30-day cycle; downstream diligence file confirming the genuine commercial relationship of each third-party payee and absence of circular or non-commercial routing.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions are routed by SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA Credit Transfer where the remitter is EEA-based) with the SCSp's full name and RCS registration number in field 70 (Remittance Information) and, for SEPA ISO 20022 pain.001, ExternalPurpose code SUBS (Subscription) or an explicit description 'capital contribution to Luxembourg SCSp under capital call dated [X]'. The receiving Luxembourg bank verifies the package comprising the capital call notice, executed LP subscription agreement, RCS excerpt, UBO declaration, and balance-of-payments statistical identification for BCL reporting. Inbound USD subscriptions are credited via the bank's New York correspondent through CHIPS/Fedwire into a multi-currency account, or converted into EUR through T2/LIPS-Gross; no BCL authorization is required, but the supporting dossier must be retained for the statutory AML/CFT period of at least five years.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: (1) Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C) issued by the Luxembourg account bank in favor of the lithium carbonate producer under UCP 600, with settlement by negotiation against presentation of a full set of clean-on-board ocean bills of lading, signed commercial invoice, certificate of origin, insurance certificate, packing list, and laboratory certificate of analysis; EUR-denominated L/Cs settle over T2/LIPS-Gross and USD-denominated L/Cs over CHIPS through the New York correspondent. (2) SWIFT MT103/MT202 wire transfers for operational settlements, freight, processing fees, and insurance premiums, with EUR via SEPA/T2 and USD via Fedwire/CHIPS. (3) Standby L/Cs or advance-payment guarantees may be issued to secure supplier prepayment terms. Every transfer carries an ISO 20022 purpose code (COMC for commercial goods; CARG for carriage/freight) and the full underlying trade package is retained for five years for CSSF/BCL inspection readiness.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD outright FX forward concluded with a Luxembourg-licensed credit institution or EU investment firm under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with the 1998 FX and Currency Options Definitions, used to hedge firm-price USD procurement commitments of battery-grade lithium carbonate.
EUR/USD FX swap (simultaneous spot purchase and forward sale, or reverse) applied to align USD disbursement peaks with L/C maturity dates while reducing counterparty credit-line usage.

EUR/USD cross-currency swap for multi-year offtake contracts converting committed USD liability streams into EUR, available subject to credit support annex (CSA collateral) or a parental guarantee from the general partner or affiliated limited partners.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) for producer-country currencies (e.g., Chilean peso, offshore renminbi) where an onshore deliverable market is unavailable to the SCSp, with cash settlement in EUR/USD and appropriate credit support; NDF is unnecessary for EUR/USD itself as the market is fully deliverable.

Exchange-traded commodity derivatives (CME Group and LME lithium contracts) permitted solely for price-risk hedging of the physical inventory and fixed-price purchase agreements, with operational segregation and compliance with EMIR clearing, margin, and reporting obligations; physically settled FX forwards and FX swaps are exempt from the EMIR mandatory clearing obligation for a non-financial counterparty such as the SCSp.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS Confirmation (Confirmation Annuelle) of registered particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés / Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS/LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Every calendar year between 1 January and 31 March; newly registered entities must complete the first annual confirmation by the first 31 March following the date of initial registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm by 31 March triggers an RCS formal notice; continued default of about two months after the notice may lead to ex officio strike-off from the RCS and publication in the electronic gazette (RESA); administrative monetary penalties up to EUR 5,000 may also be imposed, and the managing general partner remains personally liable for obligations arising during the period of non-compliance.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate (17.00% ordinary CIT + 7.00% solidarity surcharge on CIT + up to 6.75% Luxembourg City communal business tax); the SCSp itself is fiscally transparent and not in the charge to CIT.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to a trading/intermediate SCSp. The effective rate is governed by pass-through taxation: a corporate partner pays 24.94%; an individual partner pays progressive rates up to 45.01%. The participation exemption and treaty credits can reduce the effective rate on foreign-source dividends/capital gains to nil or near-nil. CIT losses may be carried forward indefinitely at partner level; the 5-year ceiling in the schema applies only to communal business tax on a commercial Luxembourg PE.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 100 (annual Luxembourg income tax return adapted for transparent partnerships), together with an annex for SCSp partner allocation; e-filing is mandatory for commercial entities via MyGuichet.lu/ACD e-space (Administration des contributions directes).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (provisional quarterly instalments of partner-level tax may be required; no quarterly CIT return is filed for a pass-through SCSp).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is 31 May following the calendar/tax year (within 5 months of fiscal year-end); e-filing extensions are discretionary and require prior request to the ACD.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SCSp identification: legal name, RCS registration number, registered office, legal form, and trade register extract.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify all non-resident special partners and their foreign tax jurisdiction; a non-resident special partner who engages in management triggers unlimited liability and must be treated as a resident commercial partner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period: start and end dates of the financial year; currency and functional currency of books.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the same accounting year as the foreign parent/counterparty to ease recognition of deferred procurement costs; non-resident partners must not create a separate Luxembourg accounting year without ACD approval.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial result before partner allocation: gross profit from battery-grade lithium carbonate purchases/sales, warehouse logistics costs, foreign exchange gains/losses, and operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the full trading result as Luxembourg-source commercial income; treaty relief depends on whether the non-resident partner has a Luxembourg permanent establishment or commercial determinative agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Arm's length transfer pricing annex: intercompany sales margins, procurement fees, commissions, financing charges, and shareholder expense allocations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must prepare OECD TP documentation (Local File/Master File) if material; commodities benchmark using CUP/TNMM; failure may lead to deemed profit adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding taxes and foreign tax credits: Luxembourg source withholding taxes, foreign withholding taxes on upstream dividends/interest, and recoverable tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach foreign tax authority certificate (TRC) and underlying beneficial ownership statement; credits flow through pro-rata to SCSp partners; non-resident partners may claim credit in home jurisdiction.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing beyond one month attracts a 10% late tax surcharge plus monthly default interest of 0.6% (intérêts moratoires); administrative fines up to EUR 4,000 per omitted annex; negligent understatement penalties 10%-25%; tax fraud is punishable by criminal penalty up to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment up to two years.
